request.spec:
A person's name must be unique on the sheet, comparing without regard to case and ignoring
spaces before and after the name. Names are stored with those surrounding spaces removed and
shown that way. Adding or editing a person to a name already in use is refused with an error on
the form, and nothing is saved.

agent.result_text:
A person's name is now unique on each sheet, ignoring case and surrounding spaces, and `bin/e2e` passes.

- **Server** (`PersonService` and `PersonRepository`): before adding or editing a person, the app checks whether another person on the sheet has the same trimmed name, ignoring case. If one does, it refuses with a 409 and saves nothing. When editing, the person's own current name doesn't count as a clash. The server already removed surrounding spaces before saving, so names are stored and shown trimmed.
- **Stored data** (new `V4__person_unique_name.sql`): this trims any existing names and adds a database-level rule so two people on a sheet can't have the same lowercased name. That rule backs up the server check if two users add the same name at the same moment.
- **Front end** (`people.ts`): when the server refuses a name, the form shows "That name is already in use on this sheet." in `person-form-error`. Other failures still show the general "Could not add/save that person." message.

Two things to know:
- **Simultaneous adds:** if two users add the same name at the same instant, the database rule rejects the second one. That user gets the general error message rather than the "already in use" one, but nothing extra is saved.
- **Existing duplicates:** the new database step would fail on a sheet that already holds two people whose names match. The database here is in-memory and starts empty on every run, so this only matters if the app is ever pointed at a store with existing data.
